commentary: On October 20, DCE i2601 Iron Ore Futures Contract closed at 767 yuan/mt, down 0.58% from the previous trading day. Spot cargoes at major ports fell by 1–5 yuan/mt, with PB ﬁnes transacƟon prices in Shandong region ranging between 775–778 yuan/mt, down 1–5 yuan/mt WoW from last Friday, while transacƟon prices of PB ﬁnes at major ports in Hebei region stood at 780–785 yuan/mt, also down 1–5 yuan/ mt WoW. Steel mills mainly procured based on demand for restocking, and market trading senƟment remained moderate. Fundamentally, narrowing steel mill proﬁts, coupled with expectaƟons of Ɵghter environmental protecƟon-driven producƟon restricƟons in some regions, have strengthened mills’ willingness to conduct maintenance, weakening support for iron ore demand. Supply side, both shipments and port arrivals increased signiﬁcantly this week, and supply is expected to remain relaƟvely ample in the near term. In the short term, with fundamental support weakening, iron ore prices are projected to ﬂuctuate.
